card.name: Sentence breaks after NSAID risk statements
card.fires_on: The period or first word of the next sentence right after a statement of NSAID or JAK-inhibitor risk, such as bleeding events, fatal cardiovascular events, or short-term therapy not being risk-free.

modes.label: Period after risk claim
modes.description: The full stop ending a sentence that says NSAIDs may increase risk of bleeding or cardiovascular events.
modes.example: NSAIDs, including meloxicam tablets, may increase the risk of bleeding events<<.>> Co-morbid conditions such as co

modes.label: Start of next risk sentence
modes.description: The first word of a new sentence that follows a risk sentence and opens a risk heading or comparison.
modes.example: However, even short-term NSAID therapy is not without risk.<< Risk>> Factors for GI Bleeding, Ulcer

card.writes: It seems to discourage 'effect'-type words after the sentence break, so a new sentence does not start with effects wording.
card.plain: It marks the point just after a warning sentence about NSAID or similar drug risks ends and a new sentence begins.
